messages:
perf-canary-bot: :warning: Perf Canary failure on `redwood/runtime` main
Job: `tiered-batching / h100 / llama3.1-70b / fast`  
Status: FAILED (p95 regression)
Run: https://github.com/redwood/perf-canary/actions/runs/9312041187  
Report: https://benchmark-lab.redwood.ai/reports/2025-02-28/perfcanary_9312041187 (table: "tier_compare")
Diff target: `main` vs `PR #18527` (scheduler workload-signal refactor)
Regression summary: p95 +18.7% (threshold 10%), queue_delay_p95 +6.2ms, gpu_util -4%

Rina Kobayashi: Seeing this too. It’s failing only on fast tier, non-streaming runs. Standard + cost-efficient look within bounds.
Linking the specific row: https://benchmark-lab.redwood.ai/reports/2025-02-28/perfcanary_9312041187#llama3.1-70b-h100-fast
Anyone know if #18527 changed the queue delay clamp logic?

Sofia Ivanova: ^ yep, #18527 moved the workload signal calc earlier and changed the default prompt bucket when missing histogram (it now falls back to p50 bucket vs “unknown”). Might be picking a bigger `max_queue_delay_ms` than intended for fast.
Can someone paste the effective config from the report?

Marcus Reed: In the benchmark-lab output it says:
- fast tier effective: `max_batch_tokens=8192`, `max_queue_delay_ms=14`, `prefill_weight=0.45`, `decode_weight=0.55`
Baseline was `max_queue_delay_ms=6` for fast on this model.
So yeah, that explains p95.

Grace Kim: Confirming baseline numbers from last green run (Feb 26): https://benchmark-lab.redwood.ai/reports/2025-02-26/perfcanary_9301127721#llama3.1-70b-h100-fast
Queue delay p95 stayed under ~5ms there.

Sahana Iyer: Any chance this is measurement flake? The run also has elevated variance on p95. But the delta is pretty big.
Also note: perf-canary worker 3 had a retry due to "runner preemption". Could rerun to be safe.

Julian Moore: From tracing on the canary job, queue wait is real. Batch formation is slower (fewer small batches), then you get tail latency spikes.
If the fallback bucket is wrong, we should fix that rather than arguing about thresholds.

Sofia Ivanova: Agree. Two actions:
1) Rerun the canary to rule out noise
2) Marcus/I can patch fast tier clamp so fallback bucket doesn’t inflate queue delay.

Rina Kobayashi: I can rerun. Do we want full suite or just the failing matrix?
Current failing set in the action: `llama3.1-70b`, H100, fast, non-streaming, conc=32/64.

Marcus Reed: Just the failing matrix is fine. If it’s still red, we can add one extra point on A100 to see if it’s SKU-specific.

Rina Kobayashi: Kicking rerun now with the same parameters + add `a100-80g` fast conc=32.
Using the workflow dispatch.
https://github.com/redwood/perf-canary/actions/runs/9312214502

perf-canary-bot: :hourglass_flowing_sand: Rerun started (workflow dispatch)
Run: https://github.com/redwood/perf-canary/actions/runs/9312214502

Sofia Ivanova: While that runs, I’m looking at the #18527 change: `queue_delay_ms = clamp(base + bucket_adj, min, max)` now uses `bucket_adj=+8` when bucket is assumed “medium”. Previously “unknown” used `bucket_adj=0`.
We should flip unknown -> “small” for fast tier, or treat missing histogram as conservative (lower queue delay).

Marcus Reed: I can put a quick fix behind the feature flag:
- if `prompt_len_bucket` missing AND tier==fast => force bucket="small".
- also cap fast `max_queue_delay_ms` at 8 for llama3.* family unless explicitly overridden.
Will send a PR shortly.

Grace Kim: Please include a unit test for the missing histogram path. That’s bitten us before.

Sahana Iyer: +1. Also can we add the effective config as an artifact to the perf-canary job? It’s in benchmark-lab but would help quickly triage.

Julian Moore: It exists via the `/explain` endpoint now, but perf-canary doesn’t call it. Could be a follow-up.
For now, bench report has “effective config” table if you expand.

perf-canary-bot: :warning: Rerun update
`llama3.1-70b / h100 / fast / non-streaming / conc=64` still failing. p95 regression +17.9%.
Preliminary report: https://benchmark-lab.redwood.ai/reports/2025-02-28/perfcanary_9312214502

Rina Kobayashi: Not a flake. A100 point also shows +12-14% p95 (still under threshold on A100 because baseline is higher, but direction is same).
So likely logic issue.

Sofia Ivanova: Ok, let’s treat this as real. Marcus, please go ahead with the fix. I’ll comment on #18527 and block merge until green.

Marcus Reed: On it. Will post PR in ~30m. Targeting just the fallback bucket + fast cap for llama3.*.

Grace Kim: Once PR is up, I can run a targeted benchmark-lab sweep (conc 16/32/64) to confirm before we burn another canary cycle.

Rina Kobayashi: Works for me. After sweep confirms, I’ll re-run perf-canary on the PR branch.

Sahana Iyer: Can we also note in the PR description: “perf-canary failing run IDs” so it’s easy to link back.

Julian Moore: Adding one more datapoint: the queue_delay histogram shifted right by ~7ms; decode stage latency unchanged. So we’re not GPU-bound; it’s purely admission/queue.

Sofia Ivanova: Thanks. Let’s keep the fix minimal and avoid changing prefill/decode weights in this patch.

Rina Kobayashi: Ack. I’ll hold off on more reruns until PR exists. Ping me when the branch is ready.
